bib.title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory
bib.venue: AAAI-24 (Thirty-Eighth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence)

question: How can LLMs be given a long-term memory that stores, retrieves, updates (with forgetting) and builds a user portrait, for sustained companionship use?
hypothesis: A memory store with dense retrieval, hierarchical summaries and Ebbinghaus-style decay lets LLMs recall past interactions and adapt to user personality.
contributions: Introduce MemoryBank, a human-like long-term memory mechanism to store, recall, update memory and draw user portrait.
Demonstrate it via SiliconFriend, an AI companion tuned with psychological dialogs.
Show generalizability: open and closed-source LLMs, English and Chinese, with and without forgetting mechanism.

method.summary: MemoryBank stores timestamped dialogs, LLM-written daily and global event summaries and personality summaries; retrieves with a DPR-style dual-tower encoder over FAISS; updates memory with R=e^(-t/S). SiliconFriend wraps ChatGPT, ChatGLM and BELLE (the last two LoRA-tuned on 38k psychological dialogs) and is evaluated on simulated 10-day dialogs with 194 probing questions.
method.task: long-term memory for dialogue agents (AI companion)

datasets.name: Psychological dialogues
datasets.source: parsed from online psychological QA websites, e.g. xinli001.com; licence not stated

datasets.name: Simulated memory storage
datasets.size: 10 days, 15 virtual users, 450 topics, at least two topics per day
datasets.source: ChatGPT generates user meta-information and plays users given topics and personalities

other.pretraining: approximately one trillion tokens of Chinese and English text

training.objective: inferred: supervised dialogue tuning with LoRA (y = Wx + BAx), open-source models only

inference.prompting: Retrieved relevant memory, global user portrait and global event summary organised into the conversation prompt; meta prompt shown in Fig 1
inference.retrieval: dual-tower dense retrieval like DPR; memory pieces (each dialog turn and event summary) pre-encoded and indexed with FAISS via LangChain; top-k and similarity threshold not stated

parameters.forgetting: R = e^(-t/S); S discrete, init 1 on first mention; on recall S += 1 and t reset to 0

metrics.name: Memory Retrieval Accuracy
metrics.definition: whether related memory is retrieved (no=0, yes=1)

metrics.name: Response Correctness
metrics.definition: response contains correct answer (wrong=0, partial=0.5, correct=1)

metrics.name: Contextual Coherence
metrics.definition: response coherent with dialogue context and retrieved memory (not=0, partially=0.5, coherent=1)

metrics.name: Model Ranking Score
metrics.definition: s = 1/r, r=1,2,3 rank among the three variants for the same question

baselines: No no-memory baseline or memory-method baseline in quantitative study
eval.protocol: Human annotators score retrieved memories and responses; number of annotators, agreement, and seeds not stated; no significance test.

prompts.text: Summarize the events and key information in the content [dialog/events]
Based on the following dialogue, please summarize the user's personality traits and emotions.[dialog]
The following are the user's exhibited personality traits and emotions throughout multiple days. Please provide a highly concise and general summary of the user's personality[daily Personalities]

results.claim: SiliconFriend-ChatGPT scores highest on response correctness in English.
results.setup: 97 English probing questions over 10-day, 15-virtual-user simulated memory; human annotators; baseline is best open-source variant (BELLE)
results.table: Table 2, English, row SiliconFriendChatGPT, column Cor.

results.claim: SiliconFriend-ChatGPT scores highest on contextual coherence in English.
results.setup: English test set; baseline is ChatGLM variant
results.table: Table 2, English, row SiliconFriendChatGPT, column Coh.

results.claim: SiliconFriend-ChatGPT has the best ranking score in English.
results.setup: English test set; ranking of three variants; baseline is BELLE variant
results.table: Table 2, English, row SiliconFriendChatGPT, column Rank

results.claim: SiliconFriend-ChatGPT has the lowest retrieval accuracy of the three variants in English.
results.setup: English test set; baseline is BELLE variant; retrieval is binary yes/no
results.table: Table 2, English, row SiliconFriendChatGPT, column RA.
results.note: Paper does not comment on ChatGPT having lowest retrieval accuracy; the open-source variants differ in embedding model (MiniLM/Text2vec) and the ChatGPT embedding is not stated.

results.claim: SiliconFriend-BELLE has the highest retrieval accuracy in Chinese.
results.setup: Chinese test set; baseline is ChatGPT variant
results.table: Table 2, Chinese, row SiliconFriendBELLE, column RA.

results.claim: In Chinese, BELLE variant beats ChatGPT variant on correctness.
results.setup: Chinese test set; value is BELLE; ChatGPT is higher (0.655), so BELLE does not win correctness in Chinese
results.table: Table 2, Chinese, row SiliconFriendBELLE, column Cor.
results.note: ChatGPT 0.655 is higher than BELLE 0.603 on Chinese correctness; the paper's text says BELLE 'excels in Chinese' but ChatGPT leads on correctness, coherence and rank in Chinese.

results.claim: Memory strength S starts at 1 on first mention and increases by 1 with t reset to 0 on each recall.
results.setup: Ebbinghaus-inspired updater R = e^(-t/S); authors call it exploratory and highly simplified
results.quote: We increase S by 1 and reset t to 0, hence forget it with a lower probability.

results.claim: Psychological tuning data size and LoRA settings for open-source variants.
results.quote: We set LoRA rank r as 128 and train the model for 3 epochs with an A100 GPU.

results.claim: Evaluation memory: 450 topics, 15 virtual users, 10 days, 194 probing questions (97 En, 97 Zh).
results.setup: ChatGPT role-plays users to generate dialogs; questions manually written
results.quote: we manually write 194 probing questions (97 in English and 97 in Chinese)

results.claim: The empathy and memory-recall comparisons against ChatGLM are shown only as single qualitative examples (Figs 2-4), with no quantitative empathy metric.
results.setup: Real-user conversations from an online platform; number of users/dialogs not stated
results.quote: we compared the responses shown by SiliconFriend with that of the baseline LLMs in real-world conversations.

limits: Forgetting mechanism is described as 'exploratory and highly simplified'; its effect is never ablated or measured (no with/without forgetting result despite the contribution claim).
Quantitative evaluation is on ChatGPT-simulated users over only 10 days, 97 questions per language; no real-user quantitative data and no baseline without memory or with another memory method.
Human annotators: number and agreement not reported; no significance tests or seeds.
Empathy gains from psychological tuning are shown only through anecdotal examples (Figs 2-4).
Retrieval hyperparameters (top-k), LoRA lr/batch size, decoding settings and ChatGPT version are not stated; no code link in the text.
ChatGPT variant has lowest retrieval accuracy; Chinese results favour BELLE on retrieval but ChatGPT on other metrics.
